steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Only menus and dialogs float; cards use lines.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Subtle shadows keep the grid crisp.

steps.use: elevation.overlay and a dimmed page for dialogs
steps.why: Floating things need a shadow so they read as on top.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.25:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So experts see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by an 8px offset and a 24px blur at 16% under the panel's edge. So a menu reads as above the grid without a heavy edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are subtle (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light shadow's shape for menus and dialogs in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 8px offset and 24px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still lifts off the dark page, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.question: How large is body text?
steps.why: Small body text fits more rows on the screen.

steps.question: What is the smallest target?
steps.why: Mouse and keyboard; compact targets are enough.
Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed reuses hover; experts do not need more.

steps.question: How fast does feedback feel?
steps.why: Fast feedback keeps up with experts.
Fast feedback confirms the pointer without slowing experts.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.1:1 on surface.default and 1.37:1 on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 7.08:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.question: What contrast floor do we hold?

steps.why: Keyboard users must always see where they are.

steps.pick: violet.light.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 6.97:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: violet.dark.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 7.62:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed reuses hover; experts do not need more.

steps.rule: Text and icons of a control that cannot be used right now.
steps.pick: neutral.500: 4.66:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. Disabled text has no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.500: 10.58:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. Disabled text has no contrast minimum.

steps.question: How many signals carry each meaning?
steps.why: Many statuses share one table; color alone is not enough.

steps.use: Button secondary, then confirm in a dialog with Button danger
steps.not: button primary as the first step
steps.why: Deleting is rare and costly; a confirm step catches mistakes.

steps.rule: Real risk: errors, failed checks, actions that cannot be undone. The top of the urgency order. Overuse wears it out.
steps.pick: red.light.600: danger reads as text and icons, 5.63:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: red.dark.600: danger reads as text and icons, 7.28:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: What separates groups on the page?
steps.why: Thin lines guide the eye along rows.
Lines separate without taking room from the data.

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.22:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.46:1, on surface.raised). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
